content: The dissertation says that in his late twenties, at his elder brother's insistence, Ibn Turka began a fifteen-year period of study abroad, roughly 795-810/1393-1408. He is reported to have spent time in Mecca and Baghdad, but the extended residence in Cairo left the deepest mark on his thought.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I 170; II 203
